interest: Letters rogatory in Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha v. United States, plus a misfiled Nagoya report.
overview: This file (decimal 894.045, May 23, 1938 – November 27, 1939) documents the legal procedures and diplomatic channels required for the procurement of judicial evidence and witness depositions in Japan for use in foreign courts. Centered on Japan's Law for Reciprocal Aid in Compliance with the Requests of Foreign Courts (Law No. 63 of 1905, as amended in 1912 and March 1938), the file begins with despatches from the American Embassy in Tokyo analyzing how Japanese law prohibits foreign consular and diplomatic officers from directly executing judicial commissions, restricting evidence taking exclusively to Japanese courts unless superseded by treaty. The bulk of the correspondence tracks a practical test case handled by the Los Angeles law firm Harper & Harper for the litigation Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha, Ltd. v. United States in the U.S. Customs Court, following the letters rogatory through diplomatic transmission, Japanese translation, execution before the Kobe Local Court for witness Gizo Sakaguchi, and final financial accounting and fee refunding. The bundle concludes with an erroneously filed 1927 consular report fragment from Nagoya discussing local political dynamics between the Minseito and Seiyukai parties, specifically examining the careers of Nagoya Mayor Isao Oiwa and Aichi Governor Toyoji Obata.

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew transmits and analyzes the March 19, 1938 amendment to Japan's Law for Reciprocal Aid in Compliance with the Requests of Foreign Courts.
subfiles.summary: Grew sends a translation of Japan's March 1938 amendment to its judicial aid law, letting treaties override its conditions on taking evidence.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2947 from Grew (Tokyo) on Amendment to Judicial Aid Law

subfiles.about: English translation of Imperial Law No. 17 amending Article 1 bis of Japan's Law for Reciprocal Aid in Complying with Requests of Foreign Courts.
subfiles.from: Prince Fumimaro Konoe, Koki Hirota, Suehiko Shiono
subfiles.summary: Translation of Law No. 17 of 1938: treaty provisions override the judicial aid law.
subfiles.title: Translation of Imperial Law No. 17 of 1938 Amending Judicial Aid Statute

subfiles.about: English translation by counsellor Tsunejiro Miyaoka of Japan's original 1905 statute governing judicial assistance to foreign courts as amended in 1912.
subfiles.summary: Translation of Japan's 1905 law on judicial aid to foreign courts, with its six conditions.
subfiles.title: Translation of Law No. 63 of 1905 for Giving Judicial Aid upon Request of Foreign Courts

subfiles.about: The State Department returns an unexecutable commission and instructs counsel on the necessity of issuing letters rogatory for execution by Japanese courts.
subfiles.summary: State returns an unexecuted commission to Harper & Harper, explaining that Japan requires letters rogatory through its courts.
subfiles.title: Letter from State Department to Harper & Harper Returning Unexecuted Commission

subfiles.about: Harper & Harper transmits Customs Court letters rogatory and a $100 cashier's check to the State Department for execution in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Harper & Harper send letters rogatory to take Gizo Sakaguchi's testimony in Kobe, with a $100 deposit.
subfiles.title: Letter from Harper & Harper Transmitting Letters Rogatory and Deposit

subfiles.about: Instruction transmitting the Customs Court letters rogatory and cost deposit to the American Embassy in Tokyo for execution through the Japanese Foreign Office.
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 1745 tells the Tokyo Embassy to present letters rogatory for Gizo Sakaguchi's testimony.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1745 to American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim (Tokyo) on Letters Rogatory
subfiles.to: American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo

subfiles.about: The State Department notifies litigation counsel that their letters rogatory and deposit have been forwarded to the American Embassy in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: State tells Harper & Harper the letters rogatory went to Tokyo; execution may take three to six months.
subfiles.title: Letter from State Department to Harper & Harper Acknowledging Transmission of Letters Rogatory

subfiles.about: Chargé Dooman transmits the completed letters rogatory and translated testimony of Gizo Sakaguchi, detailing the translation and court expenses incurred.
subfiles.summary: Dooman returns the executed letters rogatory with Gizo Sakaguchi's deposition, noting translation costs of 95 yen.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4156 from Dooman (Tokyo) Transmitting Executed Letters Rogatory

subfiles.about: Note verbale from the Japanese Foreign Ministry returning the executed letters rogatory and witness testimony of Gizo Sakaguchi and requesting fee reimbursement.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Foreign Office returns Gizo Sakaguchi's testimony and asks for ten sen in costs.
subfiles.title: Translation of Note Verbale from Japanese Foreign Office Returning Executed Documents

subfiles.about: The State Department delivers the executed letters rogatory and translated testimony of Gizo Sakaguchi to the Clerk of the U.S. Customs Court.
subfiles.summary: State sends the Customs Court clerk the executed letters rogatory and Gizo Sakaguchi's testimony.
subfiles.title: Letter from State Department to Clerk of U.S. Customs Court Transmitting Executed Evidence

subfiles.about: The State Department informs litigation counsel of the successful execution of the letters rogatory and promises a future refund of unused deposit funds.
subfiles.summary: State tells Harper & Harper the testimony is done and the deposit balance will be refunded.
subfiles.title: Letter from State Department to Harper & Harper on Completion of Letters Rogatory

subfiles.about: The Legal Adviser's Office recommends specific textual revisions for outgoing departmental letters announcing the completion of the letters rogatory.
subfiles.summary: Legal Adviser's office suggests wording for notices to the Customs Court clerk and Harper & Harper.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Legal Adviser's Office on Phrasing of Outgoing Notices

subfiles.about: The Division of Accounts transmits a verified expenditure statement and a refund check for $77.61 to litigation counsel Harper & Harper.
subfiles.summary: Division of Accounts refunds Harper & Harper $77.61 after costs of $22.39.
subfiles.title: Letter from Division of Accounts to Harper & Harper Enclosing Refund Check

subfiles.about: Incomplete consular report analyzing local political alignments in Aichi Prefecture through the careers of Nagoya Mayor Isao Oiwa and Governor Toyoji Obata.
subfiles.summary: Misfiled extract from Consul Goodier on Nagoya Mayor Isao Oiwa and Aichi Governor Toyoji Obata.
subfiles.title: Despatch Extract from Consul Goodier (Nagoya) on Aichi Prefectural and Nagoya Politics
